# Issue #112: pointers to keys containing "~" or "/" do not resolve

Given `doc = {"~1": "tilde-one", "a/b": "slash"}`, `resolve(doc, "/~01")` raises `KeyError`,
although `"~01"` is the RFC 6901 encoding of the key `"~1"`. Keys that contain a slash
(`"/a~1b"`) are also affected in some combinations. Plain keys and list indexes work fine.

The bug is in `_decode`: RFC 6901 requires decoding `~1` → `/` **before** `~0` → `~` (a single left-to-right pass). The current code does the reverse, so `~01` first becomes `~1` and then gets incorrectly turned into `/`. Let's fix the order:
edited pointer/resolve.py

doc = {"~1": "tilde-one", "a/b": "slash", "a/b~1": "combo", "~10": "slash-zero", "01": "leading-zero"}
print(resolve(doc, "/~01"))        # -> "tilde-one"
print(resolve(doc, "/a~1b"))       # -> "slash"
print(resolve(doc, "/a~1b~01"))    # -> "combo"
print(resolve(doc, "/~10"))        # -> "slash-zero"
print(resolve(doc, "/01"))         # -> "leading-zero"
print(split("/~01"))               # ['~1']
print(split("/~10"))               # ['/0']
print(split("/a~1b~01"))           # ['a/b~1']

arguments.summary: Fixed the RFC 6901 escape-decoding order in `_decode` (pointer/resolve.py). The old code did `token.replace("~0", "~").replace("~1", "/")`, which decodes `~0` first — so a token like `~01` became `~1` after the first replace and was then wrongly turned into `/`, breaking keys containing `~` (e.g. `~1`) and combinations with `/`. Per RFC 6901, `~1` must be decoded before `~0` in a single left-to-right pass, so I swapped the order to `token.replace("~1", "/").replace("~0", "~")`. Verified against the issue's cases (`/~01` → `~1`, `/a~1b` → `a/b`, `/a~1b~01` → `a/b~1`) and the full RFC 6901 example document; the existing test suite still passes.
